newsitem.title: GERMANY: Spain must and will meet EMU goals in 1997 -Aznar.
newsitem.headline: Spain must and will meet EMU goals in 1997 -Aznar.

text.p: Spanish prime minister Jose Maria Aznar, in an interview with the weekly Die Zeit, said Spain's budget deficit would be three percent of gross domestic product this year, and that the country would meet the criteria for European monetary union.

"Our budget for 1997 is the most stringent in 20 years. We will reach without problems the Maastricht goal of shrinking the deficit to three percent of GDP," advance excerpts of the interview released by Die Zeit quoted Aznar as saying.
"Spain must and will be among the founders of currency union. The citizens are prepared for that and the government is commited to do everything necessary to achieve it."
Spain must and will meet EMU goals in 1997 =2
Spain wants a strong euro as much as Germany does, Aznar said, adding that it also opposes a flexible interpretation of the Maastricht criteria.
"I know only one treaty, which sets certain entry conditions for all. And I am working to see we fulfil these conditions," he said.
Aznar took issue with suggestions that EMU should start with a small circle of participants.
"Every country should be concerned with its own contribution and do its own homework," he said.
Spanish minister of the economy and deputy prime minister Rodrigo Rato is due to visit Bonn later on Wednesday.

German state secretary of finance Juergen Stark, without naming particular countries, on Tuesday said some aspirants should forsake the political prestige of joining EMU at the outset and wait until their economic structures are well enough prepared.
